text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Peace returns to midwestern oil town of Warri after riots last week over local government changes; protesters occupied Royal Dutch's Shell installations in nearby swamps and held hostage 127 Nigerian workers for five days.
- Military government sets up panel to audit accounts of state oil company NNPC's London office, which was closed down last week
- The 7th Organisation of African Unity (OAU) trade and tourism fair opened on Saturday in Kaduna, northern Nigeria, with eight African countries in attendance.
- At least 4,000 staff of 27 failed banks will be thrown out of work from Tuesday, government deadline for banks to recapitalise or face liquidation.
- Fuel shortages linger in Nigeria's commercial capital Lagos after two weeks. Travellers face bleak Easter.
- National Intergrated Survey of Household (NISH) shows that about 66 percent of Nigerian homes are not supplied with electricity by the state power company.
- Olubunmi Okogie, Roman Catholic archbishop of Lagos, urges the military authorities in an Easter message to release all political detainees.
